title: RAW Vitruvius IX.8.9 complete-target authoring attempts: shared motion/part references with calendar binding still open
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT A SEMANTIC TEST. A prewritten independent-family selection ranks128 exposed40–80-group paragraphs with at most45 forms; the first three whole records and all raw reader alternatives are retained. The third permits tentative globally shared MOTION/WHEEL/HOURS/ZODIAC/PART values, but no complete ordinary-argument account of all source clauses was authored. Month-hole/day equality, index progression and full mechanical coupling remain jointly unbound. No sentence-sized word macro, new source or Galen dictionary repair is introduced.

The inherited source/translation/engineering/calendar-boundary limits remain.

complete_selected_source.work: Vitruvius De architectura IX.8.9, complete paragraph in the already owned Gwilt English translation
complete_selected_source.text: 9. Thus as the phellos ascends by the action of the water, the counterpoise of sand descends and turns the axis, as does that the wheel, whose rotation causes at times the greater part of the circle of the zodiac to be in motion, and at other times the smaller; thus adjusting the hours to the seasons. Moreover in the sign of each month are as many holes as there are days in it, and the index which in dials is generally a representation of the sun, shews the spaces of the hours; and whilst passing from one hole to another, it completes the period of the month.
complete_selected_source.boundary: From 9. Thus as the phellos ascends... through ...it completes the period of the month. No clause within this paragraph is dropped.
complete_selected_source.context: The §8 chain, float/phellos, equal sand counterweight, axle and marked zodiac wheel are inherited apparatus declarations; §10 transitions to water management, and §§11-15 describe the regulator. No prior analemma construction or regulator is silently claimed to be fully translated by this paragraph.
complete_selected_source.historical_limits: Ancient work, late first century BCE; owned text is the later public-domain Gwilt English translation hosted by LacusCurtius, not a medieval witness. Exact printed edition/year and Latin variants were not collated in this bounded pass. Anaporica spelling, eighth-division references and the hydraulic explanations remain this translation branch. Physical engineering adequacy is not certified. The prior analemma construction is an explicit prerequisite outside this bounded clock description.
complete_selected_source.unaltered_source_defect: The owned complete_text has an HTML/annotation fragment in §12 after Aries, including onMouseOut. Its source bytes are retained; this separate §9 boundary does not clean or certify the full excerpt. The source writes Anaporica in §8; the old anaphoric-clock card title is not new technical evidence.

full_source_obligations: The sand counterweight descends and turns the axis.
Rotation brings greater or smaller parts of the zodiac circle into motion, adjusting hours to seasons.
Each month sign has as many holes as days in that month.
The sun-shaped index shows hour spaces.
Passing from one hole to another completes the period of a month.
preserved_source_limits: Source §9 itself is complete and owned; this draft is not yet a complete target account. The whole §8–15 parent remains byte-unchanged, including the HTML/annotation fragment in §12 and Anaporica spelling in §8.

The water-driven float rise and sand-counterweight descent are opposite motions in the stated apparatus. A calendar-only list would omit the mechanical content and is not an adequate competing whole reading.
The same axle transmits motion to the wheel; the same wheel participates in the seasonal display. A fresh unrelated apparatus for each clause would lose the proposed identity link.

The source says the index passes from hole to hole; this does not by itself prove that the water mechanism automatically advances the index once per day. A manually moved calendar pin remains a serious mechanism interpretation unless the source or a separately explicit target hypothesis fixes automation.

The supplied number of days in a month and its holes are equinumerous, but no particular month lengths, starting-hole convention, number of transitions, cyclic wrap or reset are given. No hidden calendar table or numerical flow equation is inserted.

The source translation and physical engineering are not independently certified, and no Voynich diagram is identified as this clock. The prior analemma/regulator requirements remain outside the narrowly selected §9 source passage.
The whole-word lexicons of Galen496, music, amulet or transport are not inherited or repaired. This is an independent speculative family, not confirmation by code reuse.

potential_content_consequences_if_full_b.main_consequence: Counterweight descends and the same axle/wheel move.
potential_content_consequences_if_full_b.serious_rival: A different mechanical linkage can preserve all named parts while changing the opposed motion or disconnecting the later display. That would be a complete differing content claim, not just a wrong label.

potential_content_consequences_if_full_b.same_input: A persistent wheel/index in a changed seasonal or month position
potential_content_consequences_if_full_b.main_consequence: Greater/smaller zodiac-circle portions and hour display vary with season; the index’s month holes correspond to that same month’s days.
potential_content_consequences_if_full_b.serious_rival: Fixed equal-hour display or a manually versus automatically advanced index can change the predicted display/progression while retaining most part names. Manual index motion is not automatically contradicted by the chosen source paragraph.
